title: Fleet capacity handoff notes (pre-warm & rebalance)
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes from the ad-hoc handoff session on capacity rebalancing and pre-warm strategy. This is a scratchpad for the team to align on an operational pattern for moving burstable capacity between West-Asia and EU regions for the next 6 weeks while holiday traffic ramps. Not final — meant for action items and runbook edits.

Summary (headline)

- We need a repeatable, low-touch process to move a small pool (target 40-60 A100-equivalent slots) from us-west-2 spare inventory to eu-west-1 for daytime EU peak starting 2026-05-04 through 2026-06-15.
- Short-term approach: create a dedicated pre-warm fleet in eu-west-1 with warm images + warmed nvlink cache, use continuous-batching profile "eu-dayburst-v2".
- Fallback: if capacity not available in time, apply model-level graceful degradation: lower batch size + enable local KV cache persistence for 24h.

What we observed

- Last week telemetry: ~12% increase in median request rate for EU at 10:00–14:00 UTC, token distribution skew towards <256 tokens.
- Current spare pool in west-asia region (ap-southeast-1) sits at 85 A100-equivalent units idle; west-asia to eu transfer has historically taken ~36–48h for image sync + kernel warm-up.
- Cold-start latencies when spinning new instances without pre-warm images: 3.2s median, 7.8s p95. With pre-warmed images: 0.9s median, 2.1s p95.

Decisions and rationale

1) Reserve 50 units in eu-west-1 as a pre-warmed pool (tag: eu-prewarm-50). Rationale: reduces p95 cold-starts and preserves SLO during 2–3 hour ramp windows.

2) Use short-lived migration jobs instead of full reallocation. We will snapshot custom driver kernels and push to eu mirror first, then incrementally shift container image layers using CDN-backed registry. This reduces the risk of mass failures from simultaneous reboots.

3) Autoscaler policy change for eu-dayburst-v2: raise min_replicas from 8 to 12 during 09:00–16:00 UTC and set aggressive scale-up with cooldown 30s. Keep scale-down conservative (60m) to avoid churn.

Operational checklist (owners)

- Sophie: kick off registry镜像 sync job; verify sha parity; JIRA INFRA-4281. (owner: Sophie Chen)
- Noah: staging cluster pre-warm test + perf-run (batch profiles 8/16); capture p50/p95 for tokens<256. (owner: Noah Patel)
- Maya: update autoscaler manifests in kustomize overlays and schedule. (owner: Maya Singh)
- Ethan: prepare rollback playbook & quota checks for account owner approvals. (owner: Ethan Morales)
- Priya: coordinate with Solutions Eng to update customer-facing notice for enterprise tenants who have pinned eu region capacity. (owner: Priya Nair)

Open questions / risks

- Cross-region egress costs: rough estimate shows +$7k/week if we keep steady 50-unit pool replicated for 6 weeks — finance sign-off required.
- Pre-warm image drift: how often should we refresh image layers to pick up small security patches? Proposed cadence: weekly Monday AM sync.
- Kernel compatibility: two training-of-day kernels differ by minor cuDNN optimization flags; risk of perf regression if wrong kernel used. Need compatibility test matrix in CI.

Short experiment plan (48–72h)

- Day 0 (ASAP): publish sync job; run image parity check; tag prewarm images with date.
- Day 1: spin up eu-prewarm-10; run perf test harness; log p50/p95 and memory usage.
- Day 2: scale to eu-prewarm-25; run canary routing for 5% of EU traffic with fallback to hosted API. If stable -> scale to 50.

Fallback triggers (auto + manual)

- Auto: p95 latency > 3.5s for 15m -> throttle canary and redirect to cheaper variant, notify SRE channel.
- Manual: OOM events > 3 within 30m across different nodes -> immediate rollback of prewarm images to prior snapshot and put autoscaler into conservative mode.

Runbook edits suggested

- Add a "regional prewarm" section describing: prerequisite registry parity check, prewarm tagging convention, autoscaler schedule snippet, and exact rollback steps with kubectl commands + necessary IAM scopes.
- Add cost estimation template for short-term reallocations (include egress & registry transfer).

Notes to self / rough commands

- registry-sync --from us-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --images eu-dayburst-v2:* --verify-sha
- kustomize build overlays/eu | kubectl apply -f -
- perf-harness --profile batch8 --tokens 128 --runs 100 --output s3://fleet-test-results/eu-prewarm-$(date +%F)
Immediate next steps (this sprint)

- [Sophie] Start registry sync by 2026-04-26 03:00 UTC.
- [Noah] Provide staging perf results by 2026-04-27 18:00 UTC.
- [Maya] Submit autoscaler overlay PR by 2026-04-27 EOD.
- [Ethan] Draft rollback runbook and post to #fleet-ops by 2026-04-26 noon.
- [Priya] Draft brief customer note and list of pinned tenants by 2026-04-27 noon.

Appendix (metrics snapshot)

- EU 2026-04-18 -> 2026-04-24:
  - median qps (10:00-14:00 UTC): +12% week-over-week
  - median request token length: 178 tokens
  - current regional spare: eu-west-1 = 22 units; ap-southeast-1 spare = 85 units
  - image pull cold-start: p95 = 7.8s -> prewarm p95 = 2.1s

If anything here looks off or you have better estimates for egress cost or kernel compatibility windows, flag in comments. Will consolidate and move to the infra runbook once we prove the 25->50 ramp is stable.

End of notes.
